items.title: Fengyun-1C: the 2007 Anti-Satellite Test That Filled an Orbit with Debris
items.summary: The 2007 Fengyun-1C anti-satellite test: how one strike made 3,531 tracked pieces of space debris, and how the cloud spread into a shell round Earth.

items.title: One Design for the Space Radar Map and Every Site: Bigger Targets, Clearer Choices
items.summary: Space Radar’s map and sites now share one set of controls: 44 px touch targets, a visible focus ring, reduced motion respected and one main action per view.

items.title: Free Astronomy Simulations on Real Data: 15 New Lab Simulators
items.summary: Free astronomy simulations built on real data: a Hubble diagram of 740 supernovae, the 51 Pegasi wobble, COBE’s blackbody and Kepler transits.

items.title: Free Space Games: MarsVale, the Mars Colony You Build from Instagram Comments
items.summary: MarsVale is a free 3D Mars colony game that grows with its Instagram followers: comment JOIN to move in. Plus games.spaceradar.ai, Space Radar’s games.

items.title: M87* and Sagittarius A*: Black Hole Models Next to the Real EHT Images
items.summary: M87* and Sagittarius A* drawn in 3D and compared with the Event Horizon Telescope images: shadow size, spin, the bright side, and what is still wrong.

items.title: Orbit Crew: A Space Cartoon for Kids Where the Science Is Real
items.summary: Orbit Crew is a new free space science cartoon for kids aged 6 to 8 from Space Radar. Watch Episode 0, The Silent Satellite, and see how it was drawn in code.

items.title: Methanimine on Titan: ALMA Finds a Molecule Cassini Could Only Guess At
items.summary: ALMA has detected methanimine (CH2NH) in the atmosphere of Saturn’s moon Titan, a step on the chemical road to amino acids. What was found and what it means.

items.title: Space Radar Video: Narrated Flights to the Moon, Voyager 1 and TRAPPIST-1
items.summary: Watch Space Radar’s narrated space films, from the Moon to Voyager 1 and on to TRAPPIST-1, with chapters, full transcripts and a player that does not track you.

items.title: How the Night Sky Changes Over 10,000 Years, and How to Catch Algol Dimming
items.summary: Do stars move? Watch proper motion and precession reshape the sky over 10,000 years, and learn when Algol dims, with 58 variable stars that follow the clock.

items.title: Free 3D Models of Real Spacecraft: 203 Satellites, Probes and Rovers to Download
items.summary: Download free 3D models of real spacecraft: 203 satellites, stations, telescopes, probes, landers and rocket stages as glTF files under the MIT licence.

items.title: What Is the Heliosphere? The Sun’s Bubble and Where the Voyagers Crossed It
items.summary: What is the heliosphere? The Sun’s bubble, its termination shock and heliopause, and the four points where Voyager 1 and 2 crossed them, drawn in 3D.

items.title: The First Falcon 9 Landing: Landing Zone 1, 21 December 2015
items.summary: The first Falcon 9 landing: flight 20, ORBCOMM OG2, touchdown at T+9:44 on Landing Zone 1, 21 December 2015. The clock, the pad, and what a replay flies itself.

items.title: Constellations in Other Cultures: Sky Stories from Eight Peoples
items.summary: How other cultures see the constellations: Boorong, Māori, Hawaiian, Tongan, Samoan, Chinese and Norse sky stories, tap by tap, each with its source.

items.title: How Hubble Was Deployed: STS-31 and the Release from Discovery’s Arm
items.summary: How was Hubble deployed? Discovery’s arm released it at 19:38 UTC on 25 April 1990, an orbit late after a solar array stuck. The clock and the steps.

items.title: Walk on the Moon and Mars in 3D: Real Ground at Eight Landing Sites
items.summary: Walk on the Moon and Mars in your browser: eight landing sites on real LROC and HiRISE terrain, rover driving, and the sky from Mars, Titan and Proxima b.

items.title: Sixty more craft with shapes of their own
items.summary: Release 1.4.0 adds sixty models of landers, weather satellites, Earth imagers and spent stages, built from cited metres and photographs.

items.title: Space Radar 2.0.0: What’s New in the Free 3D Map of Space
items.summary: What’s new in Space Radar 2.0.0: walk at Moon and Mars landing sites, sky stories from 8 cultures, moving stars, 15 new simulators, video and VR.

items.title: Black holes in 3D, sized to the Event Horizon Telescope
items.summary: Release 1.4.0 draws Sagittarius A*, M87* and Cygnus X-1 in 3D, with shadows that follow from their masses and match the EHT's measurements.

items.title: Eight nebulae as walls of glowing gas, dust and stars
items.summary: Release 1.4.0 draws the Lagoon, Trifid, Eagle, Omega, Rosette and three more nebulae in 3D. The light is measured, the shape reconstructed.

items.title: New Horizons at Pluto: When Was Closest Approach, and How Close?
items.summary: When was New Horizons’ closest approach to Pluto? 14 July 2015, about 12,500 km up at 13.8 km/s. The two clocks, Charon, and what a replay reconstructs.

items.title: Curiosity’s Landing: The Seven Minutes of Terror, Step by Step
items.summary: Why is Curiosity’s landing called the seven minutes of terror? The JPL clock, NASA’s heights and speeds, the sky crane, and what a replay must reconstruct.

items.title: Stars with no distance, 4 383 pulsars and the farthest galaxy
items.summary: Release 1.5.0 adds 10 224 stars with no measured distance, 4 383 pulsars, the Local Group's dwarfs, quasars and MoM-z14 at redshift 14.44.

items.title: Arrokoth, Kleopatra and nine more small worlds in their own shapes
items.summary: Release 1.5.0 draws eleven asteroids and a comet from the shape models of New Horizons, Lucy, Rosetta and radar, each on its own orbit.

items.title: Moments: a mission replayed in 3D on one clock
items.summary: Release 1.5.0 adds Moments, missions replayed in 3D on one clock. The first is Apollo 11's Saturn V from ignition to the escape tower.

items.title: Free planetarium software for a classroom with no Wi-Fi
items.summary: Free planetarium software that runs with no internet: how a school keeps its own copy of Space Radar, what a lesson looks like, and what stops working.

items.title: A solar eclipse simulator, and a clock you can drag
items.summary: A solar eclipse simulator is a clock you can drag. What obeys when you scrub time on Space Radar's live map of space, what does not, and why it says so.

items.title: A virtual space tour that begins with a family photo
items.summary: A virtual space tour should be a story, not a manual. How Space Radar's 26 narrated trips are written, and three retold, from the Moon to a dead star.

items.title: What Is in the Sky Tonight? Relearning to Look Up
items.summary: Most of us have never seen the Milky Way from home. Here is what is in the sky tonight from a city balcony, and how to read it in ten minutes.

items.title: ISS pass tonight? Ask the sky over your own street
items.summary: Is there an ISS pass tonight, and what else is up? How Space Radar's Tonight view works out the sky from a named street, and what “visible” really means.

items.title: A live satellite map that tells you when it is guessing
items.summary: Space Radar is a free, open-source live satellite map of everything in orbit. Why a map of space has to be honest and kind at once, and what that costs.
